Should a ranking be used to predict outcomes and determine the "best" team, or should a ranking be used to examine what you have accomplished and determine the most "deserving" team? back when i started my rankings I was a hard supporter of the "best" team answer. but over the years, you start to see things that don't work with ranking the "best" team philosophy. many head to head matchups appear to be ignored. I had tried to balance the 2 for a while. putting in margin of victory caps, over-weighting record, etc. finally 2 years ago I decided to completely remove score altogether from my spreadsheet. the only thing that matters is what is your record, and who you beat. This makes the spreadsheet far LESS valuable as a prediction tool, but far more valuable in ranking the most worthy teams (IMHO).

so this is my current formula (and has been the formula for the last 2 seasons)

FIRST...games against 1AA teams are scrubbed from your record (unless you lose). you don't get credit for beating a team with 30 fewer scholarship players. so no...even if you played NDSU, that game still doesn't count (unless you lose)

SECOND...the basic formula is this: (team's winning %) x (team's strength of schedule)...that's it

THIRD...the SOS formula I use is pretty much the same as what the BCS used in it's 1999 version of its formula. SOS is calculated by:

determining the cumulative won/loss records of the team's opponents and the cumulative won/loss records of the teams' opponents' opponents. The formula shall be weighted two-third (66 2/3%) for the opponent's record and one-third (33 1/3%) for the opponents' opponents record....Should a team play a Division I-AA opponent, only the losses of the Division I-AA team shall be used in determining the opponent's record or the opponent's opponents' record.

and...that's it. your record times your strength of schedule. i don't care if you eek out a 1 point win in every game or blow everyone out by 50. a win is a win is a win.
